# Plan a Difficult Conversation With Help From Any AI Assistant

**Hard conversations are easier when you've thought them through first.** This guide shows you how to use an AI assistant — ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Le Chat, or any other — as a sounding board, so you can plan your words, stay calm, and say what you really mean. It works whether you need to raise a concern, set a boundary, give honest feedback at work, or talk through something tricky at home. The AI helps you think and rehearse — it can't have the conversation for you, and it shouldn't make the decision for you. No tech skills needed, just a clear goal and about 15 minutes.

## Before you start

- An AI assistant you can type into — for example ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Le Chat, DeepSeek, or Meta AI. The free version of any of them is enough; nothing in this guide needs a paid plan.
- A rough idea of who you need to talk to and what you want to say. You don't need polished thoughts — a few messy sentences are perfect.
- About 15–20 minutes somewhere quiet, so you can think and read without rushing.

## Step 1 — Get clear on what the conversation is really about

Before you open any AI, take 60 seconds to name the situation out loud or in your head. A "difficult conversation" usually hides a few smaller questions underneath: *What exactly do I want to change? What am I feeling? What would a good outcome look like?* Try to answer each in one short sentence. The AI works much better when you give it a clear starting point, just like a friend does. If you skip this, the AI's answers will feel generic and you might feel you've wasted your time. You'll see your three short sentences sitting in a notes app, a piece of paper, or even in your head — that's enough. The clearer the picture is to you, the more useful the AI's help will be a minute from now.
💬 Example: *Situation: I want to ask my manager for a day off I was promised. Feeling: anxious, afraid of looking pushy. Good outcome: I get the day off and we agree on how future requests are handled.*
You'll know it worked when you can read your three sentences back and think, "yes, that's what this is really about."

## Step 2 — Tell the AI the situation, in your own words

Open your chosen AI — in a browser tab, a phone app, or anywhere you normally chat with it. Look for the **message box** at the bottom of the screen (a long text field, often labeled "Message", "Ask anything", or "Type a prompt"). Click or tap inside it, then describe your situation in plain, everyday language. Don't worry about sounding smart or formal — the AI responds best when you write the way you'd speak to a trusted friend. The tool will reply within a few seconds, usually with a few short paragraphs that show it understood. If you can't see a message box, look for a pencil icon, a "New chat" button, or a plus sign in the corner to start a fresh conversation. If the AI's reply feels off-topic, simply add one more sentence of context and ask your question again.
💬 Example: *I need to ask my manager for a day off I was promised three weeks ago. I feel anxious because I don't want to seem pushy, but I really need the break. I'd like a good outcome where I get the day off and we agree on a clearer process for next time.*
You'll know it worked when the AI replies with something that sounds like it understood your situation, not just your keywords.

## Step 3 — Ask for three versions of the key message

Now that the AI understands the situation, ask it to help you draft the most important part of the conversation — usually the opening line or the request itself. Specifically ask for **three versions**: one gentle and friendly, one direct and clear, and one in the middle. This matters because there's no single "right" tone for hard conversations, and seeing options side by side helps you notice which words feel most like *you*. Type your request into the same chat box and send it. The AI will usually respond with three short paragraphs, each clearly labeled or visually separated. If it only gives you one version, simply reply "Can you give me two more — one softer and one more direct?" and it will adjust. Reading them aloud is a small but powerful trick: your ear catches words that don't fit you, even when they look fine on screen.
💬 Example: *Can you write me three short ways to open this conversation — one gentle, one direct, and one in the middle? Each one should be the kind of thing I'd actually say out loud.*
You'll know it worked when you have three short options in front of you, and at least one of them sounds like something you could really say.

## Step 4 — Practice the words out loud with the AI

Pick the version that felt closest to your voice, or mix phrases from all three into your own draft. Now type your chosen script back into the chat and ask the AI to play the other person. Say something like, "Pretend you're my manager and I'll say my opening line — please respond the way you think they actually would." Take a deep breath and type the words you plan to say. You'll see the AI reply in character, and the conversation will play out in a safe space. This is rehearsal, not the real thing. If the AI's reply is harsher or softer than the real person, gently tell it ("actually, my manager is usually warmer than that — could you respond that way?") and try again. The goal is to feel the words in your mouth and notice where you hesitate, so you can adjust before the real talk.
💬 Example: *Thanks, version two feels closest to me. Can you roleplay as my manager so I can practice the opening line and see how the conversation might go? I'll go first.*
You'll know it worked when you can read your opening line out loud without stumbling, and you can imagine the other person actually replying.

## Step 5 — Save a short script and plan your opening line

A few minutes before the real conversation, open your chat again and ask the AI to condense everything into a **short script you can glance at**: just your opening line, one or two key points, and how you'd like to close. Ask it to keep the whole thing under 10 lines. The AI will reply with a tight, scannable summary. Save that reply as a note on your phone, screenshot it, or copy it into a small text file — anywhere you can find it in two seconds. Reading a script in the bathroom mirror is a small but real confidence boost, and it stops the words from disappearing the moment you feel nervous. Plan your very first sentence more than anything else: the opening is the part most people stumble on, and a clear first line usually carries the rest of the talk. Afterwards, you can come back and tell the AI how it actually went, so it helps you plan even better next time.
💬 Example: *Can you turn everything we discussed into a short script I can glance at on my phone — opening line, two key points, and a calm way to close? Keep it under 10 lines.*
You'll know it worked when you have a script that fits on one screen, and your first sentence is something you can say on one breath.

## Common mistakes

- **Polishing the script until it sounds like a robot.** If the words don't sound like you, the other person will feel it. Pick the version that feels most natural, even if it's the roughest. The fix: read every line out loud; if you wouldn't say it to a friend, change it.
- **Treating the AI's draft as a script to memorise.** This guide helps you plan, not perform. The fix: use the AI's words as raw material, then rewrite key phrases in your own voice so they feel honest in your mouth.
- **Forgetting to plan how the conversation will end.** A clear, kind closing line — "thanks for hearing me out" — stops chats dragging on awkwardly. The fix: in Step 5, always ask the AI to suggest a calm way to close.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** This same approach works for apologising, asking a landlord to fix something, talking to a teenager who's shutting down, or raising a sensitive issue with a friend. The AI just helps you find your words before the moment arrives.
- **For your business or work:** Use it before a tricky performance review, a pricing conversation with a supplier, a debt reminder email, or a difficult client call. The clearer your opening line, the less time the conversation takes and the more respect both people walk away with.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't overthink the tool choice. Use whichever AI assistant you already have an account with — the best assistant is the one that's already open in your browser tab.

## Try it now

Pick one small conversation you've been putting off — a quick message to your manager, a neighbor, a friend, or a family member. Open any AI assistant right now and write a single line: *"I need to have a hard conversation with [person] about [situation]. I want to feel calm and clear. Can you help me plan what to say?"* Read the reply, copy one phrase that feels true to you, and send the message today.
